svg.title: MN 138 Uddesavibhaṅga Sutta — The Exposition of a Summary
svg.desc: A visualization of MN 138. The Buddha’s summary states three conditions — consciousness unscattered and undispersed externally, not fixated internally, and unperturbed by not grasping — which, when they meet, leave no future arising of birth, old age, death, and suffering. Each condition is then expounded through the same formula of consciousness following after, being glued, tethered, and fettered by relishing — applied to the six sense doors, the four jhānas, and the aggregates taken as self.

g.text: Examine in such a way that consciousness is —
Then there is: no future arising of birth, old age, death, and suffering
bahiddhā viññāṇaṁ avikkhittaṁ avisaṭaṁ · cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā
yoked and fettered by relishing the sign
consciousness does not follow the sign
not glued by relishing the sign
not tethered by relishing the sign
not yoked or fettered by relishing the sign
uplifting joy and pleasure born of seclusion is the flavour that may be followed
uplifting joy and pleasure born of collectedness is the flavour that may be followed
equanimity and its pleasure is the flavour that may be followed
even the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is a flavour that may be followed
When consciousness does not run after that flavour, is not glued, tethered, or fettered by it —
the mind is not fixated internally.

text.tspan: · BY NOT GRASPING, ONE IS UNPERTURBED
the same would apply for feeling, perception, intentional constructs, and consciousness

g.text: That form then changes and becomes otherwise
regards form as self — rūpaṁ attato samanupassati
consciousness is carried along by the change
does not regard form as self — na rūpaṁ attato samanupassati
consciousness is not carried along by the change
perturbation and mental disturbance do not arise,
and the mind is not overwhelmed
na paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti
not agitated · not distressed · without longing
na cevuttāsavā · na ca vighātavā · na ca apekkhavā
UNSCATTERED EXTERNALLY · NOT FIXATED INTERNALLY · UNPERTURBED
No future arising of birth, old age, death, and suffering
